title: Card Replacement, Plan Fees and Transfer on the Mountain Dining Plans
content:
Cards on a plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range are issued to the named holder and to the dependants the plan allows, and a lost or broken card is replaced against the plan's replacement fee with the balance moving to the new card and the old card stopped at every till. A plan fee is raised only while the plan record stands in the enrolled, active, suspended or exhausted state. Plan fees are collected from the household's payment method and never taken out of the dining balance, because the balance is money the household has already paid. Where the plan allows it, a plan may be moved to another household account against the plan's transfer fee, and the balance and the bonus already earned move with it; a plan that does not allow it is cancelled and a fresh plan opened on the other account.

## The two accounts a plan keeps

A plan in the range keeps its spending power and its plan fees apart. The dining balance is money the household has already paid over, and it answers only for what the card is spent on. The plan fees owed are money still to be collected, and they are collected from the household's payment method.

| What the plan holds | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The dining balance | money the household has already paid over, which answers for what the card is spent on |
| The plan fees owed | money still to be collected, which is taken from the household's payment method and never out of the dining balance |

A plan fee is raised for the enrolment, for an extra card, for a replacement card, for a transfer or for a reinstatement.

## The state a plan must stand in for a fee to be raised

The state is read from the collective's own record of the plan before the fee is raised, and it must be one of four: enrolled, active, suspended or exhausted. A plan standing in any other state is not one against which a plan fee is raised.

## Moving a plan to another household account

| The plan | What happens on the move | What the fee is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| allows the move | the plan itself moves to the other household account, carrying its balance and the bonus it has already earned | the plan's transfer fee |
| does not allow the move | the plan is given up and a fresh plan is opened on the other account | not applicable, the plan itself not being moved |

## Replacing a card

A card reported lost or broken is replaced against the plan's replacement fee. The balance is not re-created on the new card but moves to it, so what the household could spend before the replacement is what it may spend after. The card that was replaced is stopped at every till of the collective.
